chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Miskan, who linked it up to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) that he said:
One of the happiness of a man is that his business is in his own country, his companions are righteous, and he has children whom he relies upon.
ai.seo_question: What are the three things that determine a man's prosperity according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights these three pillars of worldly success, emphasizing that local commerce minimizes risk and reliance on others, while righteous companions and capable children provide essential spiritual and practical support. This triad reflects the Shia emphasis on balancing material stability with moral integrity, ensuring that prosperity serves as a means for further obedience to God rather than a distraction.
